data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim is self-defeating: it purports to show that Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is 'defensible on his own terms' as a rational selection mechanism, yet the same claim concedes that accepting this defense 'reduces rational action to a bold guess with no inductive safety net.' A defense that concludes the defended position amounts to an undefended guess has not established defensibility — it has merely redescribed the position in terms that concede its rational indefensibility. The target thus fails to distinguish between (a) showing a preference rule is internally consistent with Popper's anti-inductive framework and (b) showing it is rationally defensible. It achieves (a) only by sacrificing (b), which is the very thing the claim promises to deliver. This is distinct from the already-raised Tichý/Miller objection: it attacks the target's own stated cost-benefit structure, not the formal definability of verisimilitude.
